title: Salvage radiotherapy with or without long-term antiandrogen therapy after prostatectomy
journal: International Journal of Radiation Oncology, Biology, Physics
population: 760 eligible men after prostatectomy with pT3N0 or pT2N0 with positive margins and PSA 0.2–4.0 ng/mL
summary: At a median follow-up of 18.9 years, 18-year overall survival was 53% with salvage prostate-bed RT plus 24 months of bicalutamide versus 43% with RT plus placebo, an absolute improvement of 9.8 percentage points (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.67–1.00). The 18-year incidence of metastatic prostate cancer was 22% vs 31%, an absolute reduction of 9 points.
criticalReview: This is unusually mature evidence for the salvage setting: adding 24 months of bicalutamide to prostate-bed RT produced a clinically meaningful 9.8-point improvement in 18-year overall survival and a 9-point reduction in metastatic disease. The trade-off is substantial androgen-related toxicity, particularly gynecomastia, which occurred in 69.7% versus 10.9% in the original report. The key contemporary question is therefore not whether long-term hormonal intensification works, but which patients still need prolonged therapy in the era of early salvage RT, PSMA imaging and shorter-duration ADT strategies.
